cases.name: quick-math
cases.gate_note: Scored outside the V1 gate 2026-09-08. Its failure mode is not one any mechanism in the tool can catch: the run performs the Hastad broadcast attack correctly, verifies the cube root is exact, and submits the recovered value one transformation short of the flag. Provenance, decoys, re-derivation and the disconfirmation review all agree with it, correctly - the mathematics is sound. It stays in the suite and in the headline solve rate because it is a real challenge the tool should eventually solve; it is out of the gate because leaving it in makes 'zero false flags' unmeetable for reasons unrelated to false-flag defense.

cases.name: pwn-intended-0x1
cases.gate_note: Scored outside the V1 gate 2026-09-09 for a structural reason, not a capability one. This is a genuine buffer-overflow challenge (overwrite an adjacent int so system("cat flag.txt") fires), but in runectl's single-container sandbox the flag file it prints is directly readable by the agent's own shell — there is no privilege boundary isolating it the way a remote CTF service does. A "solve" here therefore cannot distinguish exploitation from a plain `cat flag.txt`, so gating on it would measure nothing about pwn capability. It stays in the suite and in the headline solve rate because the pwn category should run end-to-end; it is out of the gate because a locally-vendored pwn binary cannot faithfully reproduce remote flag isolation. Faithful pwn evaluation needs a service on the far side of a boundary the agent does not already own — a V2 harness concern.

cases.name: flying-places
cases.gate_note: Scored outside the V1 gate 2026-09-09. This OSINT challenge is not solvable from the provided file alone: its answer threads through live external state (the image traces to a specific Twitter post, then to a commenter's account and the city they list) that has since rotted and is not reproducible offline. It stays in the suite and in the headline so the osint category runs end-to-end and so a future online run can attempt it, but it cannot be a gate case — the gate must be deterministic and reproducible, and this depends on the live internet at a past moment. No offline-verifiable osint challenge existed in the MIT source; this is the honest fallback flagged in the M7 plan.
